title: Introduction to Trigonometry
prerequisites: Familiarity with surds such as √2 and √3.

topics.title: Trigonometric Ratios and Standard Angles
topics.quick_summary: The six trigonometric ratios relate the angles of a right triangle to its sides, and their values at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90° must be known by heart.
topics.real_life: A ramp's steepness is quoted as a gradient, which is exactly the tangent of the angle it makes with the ground.

detailed.definition: For an acute angle θ in a right triangle: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent, and cosec, sec and cot are their reciprocals.
detailed.key_idea: The ratios depend only on the angle, not on the size of the triangle, because all right triangles with the same acute angle are similar. This is why a single table of values serves every triangle.
detailed.working_principle: The standard-angle table is generated from two triangles: the 45-45-90 triangle from a square's diagonal, and the 30-60-90 triangle from an equilateral triangle cut in half.
applications: sin θ increases from 0 to 1 as θ goes from 0° to 90°; cos θ decreases from 1 to 0.
tan 90° and sec 90° are undefined; cot 0° and cosec 0° are undefined.
sin θ and cos θ can never exceed 1 in magnitude.

points: sin θ = P/H, cos θ = B/H, tan θ = P/B; cosec, sec, cot are the reciprocals.
cos values run in exactly the reverse order of sin values.
tan θ = sin θ / cos θ; cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.
sin θ and cos θ always lie between −1 and 1.
mistakes: Interchanging sin and cos when the angle is measured from the other vertex.
Treating tan 90° as infinity in a proof; it is undefined.
topics.memory_hook: 'SOH-CAH-TOA' — and for the table, sin runs 0, ½, 1/√2, √3/2, 1 while cos runs backwards.
topics.advanced: Extending these ratios to angles beyond 90° needs the unit circle, where sine and cosine become the coordinates of a point. That extension turns trigonometry from triangle measurement into the mathematics of waves.

formulas.name: Trigonometric Ratios
formulas.formula: sin θ = P/H,  cos θ = B/H,  tan θ = P/B,  cosec θ = H/P,  sec θ = H/B,  cot θ = B/P
formulas.variables: P = perpendicular (opposite side), B = base (adjacent side), H = hypotenuse.
formulas.when_to_use: For any right-angled triangle where an angle and one side are known.
formulas.common_mistakes: Identifying the wrong side as the perpendicular when the angle changes.
formulas.shortcut: The side opposite the angle is always the perpendicular for that angle.

topics.title: Trigonometric Identities
topics.quick_summary: The three Pythagorean identities relate the squares of the trigonometric ratios and are the tools for proving every other trigonometric result.
topics.real_life: Signal processing constantly uses sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to convert between amplitude and power without knowing the angle.

detailed.definition: An identity is an equation true for every value of the variable for which both sides are defined. The fundamental identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
detailed.key_idea: All three identities are the Pythagoras theorem divided by different sides. Dividing sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 by cos²θ gives the sec identity, and by sin²θ gives the cosec identity.
detailed.working_principle: The standard proof technique is to convert everything to sines and cosines, simplify, and compare. Working on one side only, and never across the equality sign, is what examiners expect.
applications: Complementary angles: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.
Rationalising expressions such as (1 + sin θ)/cos θ using the identities.
Eliminating θ between two given equations.

points: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, cos(90° − θ) = sin θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.
Work on one side of an identity only; never operate across the equals sign.
mistakes: Writing sin²θ to mean sin(θ²); it means (sin θ)².
Using sec²θ = 1 − tan²θ instead of 1 + tan²θ.
Cross-multiplying across the equality while proving an identity.
topics.memory_hook: 'Divide the first identity by cos² for sec, by sin² for cosec' — three identities, one source.
topics.advanced: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 is the equation of the unit circle in disguise. Every trigonometric identity is ultimately a statement about points on that circle.

formulas.name: Fundamental Trigonometric Identities
formulas.formula: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1;  1 + tan²θ = sec²θ;  1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ
formulas.variables: θ = any angle for which the ratios are defined.
formulas.when_to_use: To prove identities, simplify expressions and eliminate variables.
formulas.common_mistakes: Getting the sign wrong: it is 1 + tan²θ, not 1 − tan²θ.
formulas.shortcut: Convert everything to sin and cos when a proof stalls.
